result.description:
## Telecommunications Technical Officer / Technologist
## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and detail-oriented Telecommunications Technical Officer or Technologist to join our team and contribute to the delivery of reliable, high-performance telecommunications infrastructure. This role is responsible for the design, installation, maintenance, and optimisation of complex communication networks and systems across a range of technologies. The ideal candidate brings solid hands-on technical experience, strong analytical capability, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. This position suits a proactive professional who is committed to maintaining the highest standards of network performance and service delivery.
## Key Responsibilities
- Install, configure, and maintain microwave, satellite, telemetry, and other radio and electromagnetic communication systems, ensuring all equipment operates to specification and within regulatory requirements.
- Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve network faults, performance issues, and equipment malfunctions in a timely and effective manner, minimising disruption to services.
- Integrate telecommunications networks with computer hardware, software platforms, operating systems, databases, and peripheral devices to ensure seamless end-to-end functionality.
- Monitor the ongoing performance of complex networks and communication systems, identifying trends, anomalies, and areas for optimisation before they impact service quality.
- Plan and support the development of customer access network infrastructure, contributing to capacity planning, design reviews, and upgrade programmes.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation including inventory logs, equipment records, asset statuses, and communication policies, procedures, and quality standards in accordance with organisational and regulatory guidelines.
- Provide clear technical advice and support to internal stakeholders, project teams, and end users on telecommunications systems, configurations, and best practices.
- Liaise with vendors, suppliers, and external service providers to coordinate procurement, installation activities, and ongoing service delivery, whilst monitoring contractual performance and obligations.
- Support the design and optimisation of network architecture, contributing technical input to projects aimed at improving reliability, scalability, and performance.
- Conduct routine inspections, preventive maintenance, and equipment testing to ensure network integrity and compliance with applicable standards.
- Assist in the development and review of technical documentation, including network diagrams, standard operating procedures, and incident reports.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams on telecommunications projects, providing technical expertise throughout the project lifecycle from scoping through to commissioning and handover.
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- A diploma, advanced diploma, or bachelor's degree in Telecommunications Engineering, Electronics, Information Technology, or a related field; or equivalent industry experience in lieu of formal qualifications.
- Demonstrated experience in a telecommunications technical role, with hands-on exposure to radio frequency (RF), microwave, satellite, or fixed-line communication systems.
- Solid understanding of network protocols, telecommunications standards, and systems integration principles.
- Proficiency in configuring and troubleshooting network hardware, software, and associated technologies including switches, routers, and transmission equipment.
- Experience with network monitoring tools and fault management systems, with the ability to interpret performance data and take corrective action.
- Strong documentation skills with the ability to maintain accurate records, produce technical reports, and adhere to quality and compliance standards.
- Effective communication skills, with the ability to convey technical information clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Ability to manage competing priorities, work methodically under pressure, and deliver outcomes within agreed timeframes.
- A valid Australian driver's licence, as field-based work and site visits may be required.
- Willingness to participate in an on-call roster or undertake out-of-hours work when operational requirements demand.
## Preferred Qualifications
- Relevant industry certifications such as Cisco CCNA/CCNP, CompTIA Network+, or equivalent telecommunications qualifications.
- Experience working with microwave backhaul systems, fibre optic networks, or mobile network infrastructure (2G/3G/4G/5G).
- Familiarity with Australian telecommunications regulatory frameworks and compliance requirements, including those governed by the ACMA.
- Exposure to project management methodologies and experience contributing to telecommunications infrastructure projects.
- Knowledge of ITIL frameworks or experience working within a managed services or enterprise network environment.
- Postgraduate qualifications in Telecommunications, Network Engineering, or a related discipline.
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative and highly skilled engineering team working on critical telecommunications infrastructure that makes a real difference to communities and businesses across Australia.
- Enjoy genuine opportunities for professional development, including access to industry training, certifications, and career progression pathways within the organisation.
- Benefit from a flexible working environment that supports work-life balance, with options for hybrid arrangements where operational requirements allow.
- Receive a competitive remuneration package with superannuation contributions, and access to additional employee benefits including wellness programmes and paid leave entitlements.
- Work on a diverse range of projects and technologies that will broaden your technical expertise and keep you at the forefront of the evolving telecommunications landscape.
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation

All Industries Group is an innovative, multi-disciplined design, engineering and fabrication specialist. Focusing on product supply and turnkey solutions for local, national and international clients.

All Industries Group is a family owned and run manufacturing business on the central coast of Yeppoon, Qld, with its team built with the most experienced, skillful, and committed employees, is the largest manufacturing company in Livingstone Shire.

All Industries strives to set the standard of what quality looks like in the advanced manufacturing space, through our systems and culture. We are dedicated to ensuring the business is run with its employees in mind. This is accomplished through our core values which are at the centre of everything we do. These include Quality, Teamwork, Family, Integrity, and Education.

We are seeking experienced DRAFTSPERSON/ PLANNER to join our busy workshop on a full time and permanent basis.

The role includes but is not limited to:
To carry out design and development of produce including design verification and validation.
Ensuring all work is carried out in accordance with All Industries Group policies and procedures
Calculate dimensions, weight limitations and requirements in materials
Describe production methods step-by-step (including equipment and software types to be used)
Create detailed designs with Inventor and AutoCAD software
Design diagrams, maps and layouts to illustrate workflow
Identify potential operational issues and redesign products to improve functionality
Ensure final designs comply with AS/NZ & ISO standards, regulations and quality standards
Create manuals that describe existing products’ operation, features and maintenance, eg. Dossiers, close our reports etc
Provide quotations and updates to customers when required
Creating and control of production orders following AIG’s procedures using ERP system (ITMS)
Daily update of Work In Progress (WIP), job schedule and communicate information with the rest of the production team (5 day production schedule minimum)
Liaise with the production supervisor to ensure jobs are meeting deadlines, within budget hours and are meeting Quality Assessment (QA)
Encourage and maintain acceptable QA and Key Performance Indicator (KPI)
Maintain accuracy and up to date data in AIG’s Electronic Resource Planner (ERP) System (ITMS) and server drives
Include information on project planning/management, estimation & profitability
Raise NCR’s, recommend corrective action, and offer suggestions for improvement
Participate in weekly production meetings and engineering meetings
Carry out design and development of products, including verification and validation of designs
To ensure all records, including drawing numbers etc are up to date
Develop defined scope of works for tenders and attend to site/jobs when required
To ensure all communication is engaged with internal, external and third-party contractors
To report to the Management System Manager (MSM)
Undertake training for professional development and coaching and be involved in AIG’s competitive business systems (Lean/Six Sigma)

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
At least with more than 4-years of experience in the same trade
Ability to work well both independently and in a team environment
Strong communication skills
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!

Salary: $75,000 – $90,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Payroll Officer to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Payroll Officer, you will be responsible for managing payroll processing activities, maintaining accurate employee records, and ensuring employees are paid correctly and on time. You will work closely with the finance, human resources, project, and operational teams to ensure payroll processes comply with company policies, awards, employment conditions, and relevant legislation.

Key Responsibilities
•	Process end-to-end payroll activities for employees, including weekly and fortnightly payroll cycles.
•	Maintain accurate employee payroll records, including salaries, allowances, deductions, leave balances, and employment details.
•	Verify timesheets, overtime, allowances, leave applications, and payroll adjustments.
•	Ensure payroll calculations comply with relevant awards, enterprise agreements, employment contracts, and legislation.
•	Process new employee onboarding, payroll setup, and employee changes.
•	Manage employee queries relating to payroll, leave entitlements, deductions, and payments.
•	Prepare payroll reports, reconciliations, and supporting documentation for management and finance teams.
•	Process superannuation payments, payroll tax, PAYG withholding, and other statutory obligations.
•	Maintain accurate records and assist with payroll audits and compliance reviews.
•	Liaise with HR, project managers, supervisors, and employees regarding payroll-related matters.
•	Assist with improving payroll processes and maintaining payroll system accuracy.
•	Ensure confidentiality and security of employee payroll information.
•	Follow workplace health and safety policies, company procedures, and quality management systems.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1–2 years of full-time experience as a Payroll Officer or in a similar payroll/finance administration role.
•	Experience processing payroll in a medium to large organisation is highly regarded.
•	Strong understanding of payroll processes, employment conditions, and statutory requirements.
•	Experience with payroll software and Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
•	Strong attention to detail and accuracy in handling financial and employee data.
•	Excellent organisational and time management skills.
•	Ability to manage confidential information professionally.
•	Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively with employees and management teams.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $75,000 – $90,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work within a growing mining and industrial services organisation.
•	Ongoing training and professional development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

Be part of a company that’s in the action!

Integra Water Treatment Solutions is a national, Australian owned company who specialize in commercial and industrial water treatment.  Our company has grown from humble beginnings in 1990 to now including 200 plus in our team Australia wide. Our Sydney operation is currently seeking expand the team with a motivated and enthusiastic person to be included our small but experienced team, specialising in water & wastewater treatment, reuse and environmental treatment systems & applications.  

Integra offer expertise in the following areas:
•	Cooling water treatment and tower cleaning
•	Boiler water treatment
•	Pre-treatment, filtration and desalination
•	Waste water treatment
•	Equipment design, repair and installation
•	Cleaning and hygiene solutions


Water & Wastewater Operations: Environmental Consultant 
To be successful in this role you will have experience in working in a team, have good interpersonal and communication skills and be self-motivated. You will have had experience with meeting scheduled customer wastewater service requirements and co-ordinating multiple and competing requirements to limited time frames.

Role Description:
•	Designing strategic environmental action plans to guide sustainable water and wastewater management across Integra Water's industrial, commercial and manufacturing client sites, identifying immediate priorities and establishing long-term treatment and compliance objectives. 
•	Monitoring compliance with environmental statutes and discharge regulations governing water treatment, effluent release and re-use, and initiating corrective measures to protect waterways and surrounding ecosystems. 
•	Conducting comprehensive site assessments prior to the installation or upgrade of water treatment, filtration and wastewater infrastructure to anticipate ecological and regulatory consequences. 
•	Recommending mitigation strategies to offset the environmental impact of industrial water use and effluent discharge, and to support restoration of affected water systems. 
•	Investigating how variables such as water chemistry, temperature, flow conditions, seasonal patterns and site-specific operational processes influence treatment performance and environmental outcomes. 
•	Collecting and interpreting data from water, effluent and soil analyses to evaluate contamination levels and inform treatment, filtration and re-use strategies. 
•	Developing environmental management policies and pollution control benchmarks for industrial and commercial water and wastewater operations, including standards for the treatment of disturbed or contaminated sites. 
•	Coordinating environmental initiatives across client facilities — including manufacturing plants, food processors and commercial premises — to protect water quality and support sustainable resource use. 
•	Compiling environmental data and technical resource inventories to support Integra Water's clients in land-use, treatment infrastructure and resource management decisions.

Requirements: 
•	Relevant Qualification
•	At least 3 years of experience

About our Organisation

AVK is a highly respected global business and one of the leading valve manufacturers in the water supply, wastewater, civil infrastructure, gas, fire protection and industrial sectors. The AVK Group operates more than 100 companies worldwide, supplying to more than 80 countries and employs around 5,300 people. AVK's core business is the design and manufacture of valves, hydrants, fitting, clamps, and accessories each complying with the highest standards of quality, safety, and durability. In addition to the products, AVK Smart Water systems provide digital solutions for AVK core products through intelligent IoT-based platform as a new way for asset owners to monitor water infrastructure. 
AVK Australia is part of the Global AVK Group and responsible for the group’s activities in the Oceania region (Australia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea & Pacific Islands). AVK Australia is based in Wingfield, South Australia, with operations across Australia as well as New Zealand.

About the Role 

We are currently seeking a Governance & Commercial Legal Advisor to join our team on a permanent full-time basis. 

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Governance & Commercial Legal Advisor will be responsible for supporting organisational governance, regulatory compliance, internal controls and business risk management across the organisation.

The position provides advice and support to management and project delivery teams through risk management initiatives, analysis of organisational information and data, and implementation of processes that ensure compliance with regulatory and governance requirements.

Key Responsibilities

•	Working with Project Delivery team develop and implement systems for document control, including approvals and version controls
•	Analysis of project costs and forecasts to identify potential for variations and forecast project profitability
•	Analysing project performance data to support organisational planning, decision-making and process optimisation
•	Reviewing contracts and templates to ensure regulatory compliance and analyse to identify potential risks
•	Develop, review and maintain organisational policies, procedures, templates and governance documentation
•	Analyse and assess government and industry programs, including grant programs, and identify opportunities for the company to participate
•	Develop a "Tender Toolbox" for use in Project Tender Submissions, containing relevant Governance and Compliance documentation
•	Administration of Regulatory Compliance Program
•	Support the implementation of risk management IT systems in HSE, Quality and HR operations
•	Assist business managers to design, develop and implement corrective action programs to address legal compliance risks and / or adapt to changes in the regulatory environment
•	Analyse duty costs, identify opportunities for duty drawback claims, and administer regular claims
•	Maintain governance registers and organisational records relating to corporate assets and compliance obligations

Skills & Experience

•	A relevant Bachelor Degree or higher and a minimum of 12 months relevant experience. 5 years’ experience may be considered in lieu of qualification
•	Experience reviewing contracts, policies and governance documents 
•	Ability to analyse data and other information to support forecasting and decision-making
•	Ability to engage with stakeholders to coordinate effective organisational outcomes
•	Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities
•	Strong verbal and written communication skills

If this sounds like the job for you, then please apply now by submitting your CV and a covering letter, in Word format, addressing the selection criteria.  

Visit our website http://www.avkcivil.com.au to learn more about the company, or our global website www.avkvalves.com to learn more about the AVK Group in general.
